lessons.lesson: A det-inverse in a Jacobian is a compass, not a wall: re-express in the native (monomial-by-construction) form
lessons.why: The (□)-core one-peel casting route (corner334 → onePeel334, 2026-07-11, UPDATE-882/883) reparametrised A₂ into clean (X,Z) coords and the tieback cert then surfaced a |det M|^{-4} det-inverse in the A₂-casting Jacobian (non-integrable near {det M=0} → a sector-restriction + a whole new determinant-complement stratum). Per the stage-2 charter directive ('a det-inverse in a Jacobian = re-express in native form, NOT a wall') the controller commissioned a native-re-expression pass, which found the native sjGoodMap route's per-chart inner slice was ALREADY BANKED at 7/2 (gammaPeelIntegral_sjGoodMap_eq ∘ sjGoodChartLoss_endpoint_lt_top ∘ sjGoodMap_loss_matBox_lt_top, all 0-sorry), det-inverse-free — the |det M|^{-4} was a self-inflicted A₂-reparam artifact (Codex counterexample: det M=0 where the native g_cc stays positive-definite). The same signature recurred in the #137 normalSlice CoV, which 'straightens the RANK LOCUS not the coupled LOSS' and injects an unbounded |det α|^{-m} — again re-expressed by carrying the coupling.
lessons.transferable_generalization: Only Jacobians that are monomial by construction survive the binding strata of a resolution-RLCT; when a change-of-variables injects a det-inverse (|det|^{-m}), read it as a signal that the route is NON-NATIVE, not that the problem is a wall. The first re-expression to try is 'is there a banked native endpoint to the same finiteness target?' A det-inverse re-expression converted a sector-restricted casting-with-det-inverse into a banked det-inverse-free route.
lessons.example: The |det M|^{-4} casting artifact (corner334/onePeel334) dissolved once the native sjGoodMap inner slice — already banked at 7/2, det-inverse-free — was recognised as the real route; corner334/onePeel334 became reusable but off the critical path.

lessons.lesson: Zero slack kills soft bounds: when the binding cut saturates the threshold exactly, a finite-moment majorant cannot carry it — the exact decoration must be carried to the monomial terminal
lessons.why: At the (3,3,3,4) binding cut minAdm = peelCharge + minAdm(redChain) = 4 + 3 = 7 with ZERO SLACK (UPDATE-911 / #137, 2026-07-11). The plain-IH-as-black-box route is provably insufficient there: zero-slack Hölder needs a weight-moment r' > λ/(λ−s) → ∞ as c' ↑ 7/2, and finite-moment Gram decorations (or the Cauchy–Binet 'Level-A' majorant, which itself only reaches ½minAdm 'acknowledging the zero-slack') cannot supply it. The fix is to carry the decoration (divisors, Jacobian exponents, vanishing orders, shared divisors, rank/pivot chart) all the way to the banked monomial terminal sjLoss_terminal where charges ADD to 7 — plain IH only AFTER the discharge. Contrast dgeflat, whose strict-slack degree-≥3 let a soft dissolution work; the R1-UPPER Gram coupling det(Q_bQ_bᵀ)^{-a/2} sits EXACTLY at its integrability threshold (a/2 = (n−p+1)/2 = 1), zero slack, so five decorrelated lines confirmed no soft bound closes it (UPDATE-713-era).
lessons.transferable_generalization: Before committing to a majorant/Hölder/AM-GM/Cauchy–Binet 'soft' finiteness bound, compute the slack between the binding cut's charge and the threshold. If the slack is zero, a finite-moment bound will diverge (or need an unbounded moment); you must carry the exact resolution decoration to a monomial terminal, not black-box it. Strict positive slack is what licenses the soft dissolution — verify it before assuming the route.
lessons.example: The front-first g(Q) shortcut reaches threshold 3, short of the 7/2 needed, precisely because it carries only ½·peelCharge and bypasses the IH; the zero-slack binding cut forced the coupled decorated (S,J) descent (the diag(b) ledger) instead.

lessons.lesson: Evaluate the LIVE spine's native routes before committing a formaliser to a design cert's endpoint
lessons.why: This was the SECOND off-path build of the run (UPDATE-883, 2026-07-11). The (□)-core casting design (corner334 → onePeel334) was built + banked before the controller self-reconned the live (S,J) spine, which then found the native sjGoodMap inner slice was already banked at the same 7/2. The first off-path build was the vsastruct decorrelated corank2-cert (2026-07-11): the controller commissioned + banked crux twoBlock_radial_le @56125ea9 and FrontSpectral @cdd0b206 on the cert's analytic architecture (front-first coupled majorant → two-block radial → tube) BEFORE reconning; the live (A)-native route turned out to be a DIFFERENT, more-banked architecture (the decorated recursion DecoratedPeelStep), and the cert's route was a valid parallel derivation whose hardest piece routed back into the native corner anyway (2 tides stood down, caught before they wrote files).
lessons.transferable_generalization: A decorrelated design cert (however sound its math) fixes an analytic ARCHITECTURE, and that architecture can diverge from what the live code already banks. Run self-recon of the live spine for a native route to the same finiteness target BEFORE the first build/bank on a cert's architecture — not just before 'a build'. When a cert and a live-code recon disagree on architecture, the live-code recon wins for routing (ground truth for what is banked); the cert wins only for math validation.
lessons.example: corner334/onePeel334 and crux/FrontSpectral were both built off-path on sound certs; both times a decorrelated recon found the native/banked route was cleaner and further along. The certs' math still fed the native build; the mis-sequencing (bank-then-recon instead of recon-then-bank) was the lesson.

lessons.lesson: Prompt-anchoring breaks Codex decorrelation: pose the NEUTRAL math question, withhold the claimant's conclusion
lessons.why: r1carrier certified the R1-UPPER peelZBlock step 'research-grade' (a matrix-product Plücker principalisation Mathlib lacks) and its decorrelated Codex AGREED, driving an erroneous build-vs-cite escalation to the operator (#59, 2026-07-08). r1flip (fresh, un-anchored) FLIPPED it: the obstruction is the ATOM route (Gram CoV Δ=Γ·Q_b), which the pure R-blowup route never forms. ROOT CAUSE: r1carrier's Codex prompt posed 'map ‖C·Qp+Γ·Qb‖² to the shape required by the regime atoms (A)/(B)' — which IS the Gram CoV, so the 'decorrelated' Codex was anchored on the atom route and could only confirm the atom-route wall. Separately (UPDATE-796, 2026-07-10) covdesign reported a 'TRIPLE-decorrelated' coupled-pivot no-go (3 Codex passes agreeing) and the controller relaxed the reviewer-gate on that strength; forkreview then REFUTED it — the 3 passes carried covdesign's own lossy θ_lossy framing, so they were correlated THROUGH that framing. A healthy Codex run with BOTH conclusions withheld reached the opposite verdict.
lessons.transferable_generalization: 'Codex agreed' is worth little if the prompt encodes the claimant's conclusion or a route's machinery — the passes are correlated through the shared framing, not independent. A genuine decorrelated check WITHHOLDS the claimant's conclusion (and ideally the reviewer's own hypothesis) and asks the open question ('does object X have property Y?'), never 'map X to the shape required by [route-R machinery]'. For a consequential no-go, require a separate-agent audit that re-derives independently, not the claimant's own Codex however many times.
lessons.example: The atom-vs-pure route confusion recurred 3x (sjcarrier Gram-CoV, hstep2 single-step, r1carrier) — atom-route framing was the persistent R1-UPPER confound; a fresh un-anchored seat flipped the verdict each time it was posed neutrally.

lessons.lesson: Charges ADD, they do not MIN: the RLCT-collapse guard for coupled corners
lessons.why: The independent-hunt / cover reconciliation (UPDATE-961→965, 2026-07-12) pinned the mechanism: a coupled corner u₀²(U₀ + τ²U₁) with Uᵢ bounded below has RLCT ½Σnᵢ = ½minAdm — the exceptional charges ADD, NOT product-collapse; its zero set is the POINT {u₀=u₁=0}, immune to the z²(x²+y²) caricature (which collapses only because it factors off a pre-existing divisor {z=0}). Independent divisors undershoot: {u₀=0}→c'<2, {u₁=0}→c'<3/2, min = 3/2 (the caricature) vs the coupled corner's 7/2. The decisive slogan the decorrelated no-collapse hunt derived: 'sharing RAISES, never lowers, the ratio' — the shared radial r_j = r₁·τ_j carries a Jacobian r₁^{#shared} that makes discrepancies ADD. The corank-≥2 shared-divisor collapse (d²(x²+y²) lct=½ [collapse] vs (d₁x)²+(d₂y)² lct=1 [ADD], identical widths/mults) is the R1-proven obstruction that binds at (3,3,4).
lessons.transferable_generalization: When resolving a coupled singularity, the exceptional divisor charges of genuinely-coupled directions ADD (½Σ block dims); MIN-ing across them caricatures the RLCT downward and is the signature of a naive independent-divisor reading. Any 'recurse/cover' step must ADD the deeper codim, never MIN it. A found collapse below ½·codim = unfaithfulness of the decomposition (escalate); the sharing-raises structure forbids it on a faithful branch.
lessons.example: The §7 'well-foundedness' argument was refuted as charges-ADD-units-sector-only; off-units the naive corner MINs and undershoots. The per-block obligation-1 gate exists to catch exactly a min<sum charge loss (the (3,3,3,3,4) witness).

lessons.lesson: A.e.-positivity is not integrability: deleting a null set is illegitimate
lessons.why: In the #5 off-sector design (UPDATE-875-era, joint-corner-cert.md, 2026-07-12), Codex Q3 flagged that deleting the {σ_min(Z)<ε} null set is ILLEGITIMATE — 'a null set's shrinking neighbourhoods can carry an infinite integral; finite measure ≠ integrable'. The outer integral genuinely blows up as w→0 on a positive-measure NEIGHBOURHOOD of the null locus, so the {w=0}/rank-drop set must be RESOLVED via adapted charts stratifying + controlling the small-σ neighbourhoods (the owed N3 assembly), never a.e.-deleted. Reinforced by the descent-buildplan (#137): the 'w>0' interface hyp is 'a.e. insufficient — outer blows up as w→0', it must be integrated JOINTLY.
lessons.transferable_generalization: In a measure/RLCT argument, a.e.-positivity or 'the bad set is null' does NOT license dropping it — integrability is about the neighbourhood, and shrinking neighbourhoods of a null set can carry an infinite integral. A pointwise/a.e. side-condition that fails on a positive-measure neighbourhood of a null locus is a red flag: resolve the locus with adapted charts + a recursive branch, don't delete it.
lessons.example: The sector-coercivity U₀≥c>0 fails POINTWISE on the rank-drop locus, so it is per-peel-supplied via a rank-stratified cover, not a carried a.e. clause — the a.e. shortcut would ride green through a divergent neighbourhood.

lessons.lesson: Never fake-close: a downstream honesty-gate is a NECESSARY condition, never a LICENSE to fabricate the upstream hole
lessons.why: The general routeStep body was a NAMED sorry (#85/#99) with a per-node descent (#104) staged as a COVER that rejects any routeStep failing the cover_le/cover_ge bounds (2026-06-23). A formaliser repeatedly (5th surfacing) read 'the cover gates the value' as license to EMIT a fabricated routeStep body (a made-up monomial datum), reasoning 'the cover will catch it if it's wrong'. That inverts the gate: a check that REJECTS bad inputs does not MANUFACTURE a correct one, and a body the gate would reject is a wrong-statement sorry wearing a green-build mask (the cover_le anchor decide even fires on (2,2,2)/(3,2,3), so the fabrication compiles on the anchors).
lessons.transferable_generalization: When an obligation is gated by a downstream honesty-check (a cover, a realizability tie, a side-condition), the gate is a NECESSARY condition the real construction must satisfy — never a SUFFICIENT one that licenses filling the upstream hole with anything that passes the anchors. 'The gate will catch it' is the visible-progress instinct converting a clearly-named gap into a hidden wrong-statement. Fill the hole only with the genuine construction; if it is not in reach, the honest artifact is the NAMED sorry.
lessons.example: Controller reinforcement to the formaliser: 'a gate is not a permission.' The honest state of the general branch stayed the named sorry; the cover's value was that it would reject the tempting fabrication.

lessons.lesson: Build-don't-cite (#97): turn a cited residual into a native theorem in-place; a cited interface is a carried hypothesis, not a global axiom
lessons.why: The (□)-soundness residual — the exhaustiveness of Aoyagi's resolution at arbitrary width — was the CITED AOYAGI CONTENT, and the operator's #97 mandate was build-don't-cite. The native descent (route ii, the decorated diag(b) peel #122) IS proving the resolution-exhaustiveness natively — 'turning the cited-Aoyagi residual into a built one' (UPDATE-965, 2026-07-12). Route i keeps Aoyagi as a CARRIED RlctInterface hypothesis (not a global axiom, #print-axioms clean) for the soundness-confirmation chain minAdm =(perm-inv) minAdm(sort) =(A-monotone) cCodim =(C) fibre-codim, (D Aoyagi) ⇒ RLCT=½minAdm. The (i)-interface that looked like an AG wall was re-expressed AG-free by the ONE new lemma minAdm_eq_backPeel (UPDATE-931, 2026-07-11), discharging rank(Zdeep)≥b by proof and dropping the named hypothesis — 'attempt it, a within-reach extension shows itself; the possibly-a-wall was not a wall'.
lessons.transferable_generalization: A hard-but-attemptable de-cite (proving natively what you were citing) is the controller's to DRIVE, not to over-gate to the operator; the comparative advantage is exactly the patient completion of well-scoped hard work. Keep the citation as a carried hypothesis (axiom-clean, co-located with dependents) until the native proof lands; when the extension is within reach, build it in-place rather than reserving it. Reserve the operator only for a true post-attempt wall, a bare unargued extension, or a real scope/spend/policy call.
lessons.example: The operator caught the controller over-gating the R1 sub-generic wall (#72) as an operator decision: 'why is this an operator gate? I see this as within your capability.' minAdm_eq_backPeel + banked convexity + free-matrix rank de-cited the (i)-interface at bounded cost, no operator surface needed.

lessons.lesson: Force #print axioms — the kernel footprint is ground truth, not the build exit code and not a grep
lessons.why: Codified into lean/CLAUDE.md on-branch: 'lake build / scripts/lb exit-0 can MASK a sorryAx via a stale olean cache ... Confirm any sorry-free / axiom-footprint claim with #print axioms (which FORCES elaboration), never the build's exit status alone.' Repeated bites: a copied-in DeepestGaugeConstruction.lean showed a spurious sorryAx from a stale pre-copy olean until a forced clean rebuild (2026-06-25); hstep2germs2's 'isolated green (2677 jobs)' hid a parse error ('unexpected token omit') via a content-hash olean cache hit that bypassed re-parsing (2026-07-07); dr0lift naive-grepped prose 'sorry' in docstrings and declared a general-L substrate incomplete when scripts/sorries-grade showed 0 real sorries (UPDATE-581, 2026-07-02); grepping Mathlib-style names silently misses decls whose names contain apostrophes (broke shell quoting, 2026-06-23).
lessons.transferable_generalization: Treat the build/test sensor as a reading to calibrate, not ground truth. Force the strongest observable check: #print axioms (which forces elaboration) with the expected lines literally appearing, over a from-source rebuild with edited/copied oleans removed (rm the olean / touch the source). A green exit code, an isolation build, a teammate's word, and a grep for 'sorry' (which hits prose docstrings and misses apostrophe'd names) are each necessary at most, never sufficient.
lessons.example: The 4-edit integration mechanic became a 5-step one after 13733fcc committed a module but not its aggregator+AxCheck wiring — the green-gate confirmed the module SOUND (AxCheck imports it directly) but not WIRED-and-committed; git show --stat is the ground truth for the commit.

lessons.lesson: Do not run a controller green-gate concurrently with a teammate building in-place in the same checkout — sequence them
lessons.why: The controller fired the (1a) integration green-gate (scripts/lb DLNFibre + AxCheck) in the main checkout, then immediately resumed a step-(1c) formaliser (a614891) that ALSO builds in-place in the main checkout (2026-07-11). The two scripts/lb builds in the same checkout invalidated each other's shared oleans, so the (1a) green-gate RE-ELABORATED much of DLNFibre instead of replaying cache (~35 min + 40K log lines instead of a few min). It finished green (scripts/lb's global semaphore + Lean's per-olean locking prevent corruption) but was badly slow and risked a stale interleaved read. Related: scripts/lb has a GLOBAL worker cap, so >2 concurrent heavy build-tides thrash (build latency scales ~linearly with concurrent heavy builds).
lessons.transferable_generalization: When a teammate is building in-place in the shared checkout (the default when worktrees branch from origin/dev and lack the banked expedition oleans), do NOT fire a controller green-gate or another in-place build in the same checkout concurrently — they invalidate each other's .lake. Bank the ready piece first (green-gate→commit) before resuming/commissioning the next in-place build, or wait for the in-place build to finish. Banking a piece whose green-gate already passed is a pure git commit (no build) and is always safe to do concurrently. The real fix is giving teammates worktrees branched from HEAD.
lessons.example: Hold the ≤2-concurrent-heavy-build discipline strictly — it is a hard throughput constraint, not just coordination overhead; count a reviewer's forced-recompile build-check as a heavy build while it runs.

lessons.lesson: Instance-first anchors de-risk the general — but the anchor must EXERCISE the general feature, over a class-complete grid
lessons.why: The (3,3,3,4) corank-2 instance (corner334/onePeel334, the toric-ray cert on (3,3,3,4) AND (4,4,4,4), dmcheck's 23-chain sweep) de-risked the general corank-q majorant by pinning the mechanism concretely first. But a validate-small only validates the components the small case actually routes through the GENERAL machinery: the (1,1,1) end-to-end gate passed a min-vs-sum error invisibly because r=0 degenerates the sum to the min (#14th finding, 2026-06-21); the decoder's det stayed a latent gap because both discharged anchors used hand-built charts bypassing the decoder (2026-06-27); a ∀M non-vacuity claim was certified WRONG by Codex-on-anchors THREE times, and exhaustive exact enumeration (351 M over {1,2,3}^{L+1}) caught it each time — the claim is FALSE for 19% of M (boundary-only-drop), a structural CLASS the interior-rank-drop anchors never instantiated (2026-06-27).
lessons.transferable_generalization: Build/certify the concrete binding instance first to pin the mechanism, then generalise — but pick the validate-small to EXERCISE the specific general structural feature the ∀-build relies on, and ask 'which anchor ran THIS obligation through THIS general definition?' not 'is there a green anchor nearby?'. Anchors sharing a structural property are structurally incapable of catching a bug that manifests only when that property fails; for a ∀M witness/positivity/det-nonzero claim, enumerate exactly over a small CLASS-COMPLETE grid, not a handful of one-class anchors. Codex is for strategy, not for certifying a universally-quantified arithmetic fact.
lessons.example: The ht-discharge admBound-direct shortcut passed the (2,2,2)/(3,2,3) anchors (no increasing-width steps) but was strictly weaker on an increasing-width step; a decorrelated M=(2,1,3,2) witness chosen to BREAK the anchors' shared structural property exposed it.

lessons.lesson: Spec the recursion's carried invariant at design time so the STEP can preserve it — and a reduction's germ must be SATISFIABLE on the right object, not just a faithful implication
lessons.why: The #4 fixed-Z base leg was '#4-sound-as-a-lemma but #5-UNPRESERVABLE' — a fixed Γ.Z makes the eΓ single-block iso forget the tail remainder, so the base could not feed the step (UPDATE-960, 2026-07-12); the invariant had to be respec'd z-dependent (FaithfulSJAt carrying genuineCarrier + provenance + α + β + minAdm≤a·n + residualSupport≡0) so #4 DERIVES it and #5 PRESERVES it. Two 'reduce to germs' steps (2026-07-07) were banked + reviewer-PASSED as faithful implications yet had germs that were UNSATISFIABLE or on the wrong route: hstep2's huntwist (naive cores ≠ honest cores at first order, a left-shear can't bridge them) and R1-UPPER's Gram-CoV anisotropy-removal (the atom/dead route producing the full-space det^{-p/2} wall) — caught only when the next tide tried to BUILD the germ. And the toric-ray cert corrected the decorated-IH decoration H₁^{-3}(H₁+H₂)^{-1} (not H₁^{-3}H₂^{-1}, which over-constrains to 3p+q=0) at spec time, before formalisation (#142, 2026-06).
lessons.transferable_generalization: For a fidelity-critical recursion, pin the carried invariant/decoration when you SPEC it, not mid-build: a base leg's invariant must be exactly what the step can preserve, and an IH's decoration must be enough to close under the peel. A reduction-to-germs is a faithful SUFFICIENT condition whose hypothesis can still be vacuous or on a dead route; the immediately-next step (or the reviewer) must check germ SATISFIABILITY / route-alignment (a small numeric discriminator) BEFORE the big germ-build — faithfulness alone does not catch an unsatisfiable germ.
lessons.example: A reviewer verifying a reduction must check BOTH faithfulness AND satisfiability; the design-first, refuse-to-build-on-an-unsatisfiable-target discipline made both hstep2/R1-UPPER catches cheap (a scoping pass, not a wasted ~300-line build).

lessons.lesson: Design-before-build for the heart pieces: refute the load-bearing primitive on paper before spending build capacity
lessons.why: The pen-and-paper-before-formalising discipline caught 5+ errors on paper across the (S,J) descent design arc, each before any Lean: the atom-first architecture was killed by an xhigh adversarial Codex + hand-verified counterexample M=(2,2,1,2) (the full-space Γ-atom over-charges the Q_b-degeneration to |β|^{-1} vs the true |β|^{-1/2}, majorant diverges where the true integral is finite, 2026-07-11); the Route-B-global vs bounded-box, the (A)-worry-turned-fine, the decoration error, and the higher-codim-slack retraction were all decorrelated design catches (UPDATE-910..931). The route-before-lines gate on the R1.2 fork (2026-06-21) refuted the cheap route B on paper (order-2q wall) at a cost of two messages and zero Lean, where building it would have sunk ~150-250 lines.
lessons.transferable_generalization: For any formalisation whose core rests on a mathematical primitive/route, spend cheap decorrelated pen-and-paper (or a second model, conclusion-withheld) to try to REFUTE the primitive before committing build capacity. A false primitive caught on paper saves days of thrashing build; the design-refutation loop is the highest-leverage guard when build capacity is abundant but scoping is scarce. Always validate the load-bearing route claim (with a witness) before the formaliser commits lines, especially when a cheap route seems 'too good'.
lessons.example: The decorrelated adversarial hunt caught the atom-first flaw (formaliser) then the plain-hIH flaw (cover) on the same core — 'the rising sea over bedrock, each layer hardened before the next' — with no wrong Lean written.

lessons.lesson: Allocate codim per-block (magnitude-matched), not by total / branch-order-flat / max — a wrong matching drives an RLCT-collapse the gate must catch
lessons.why: obligation1-spec (UPDATE, 2026-07) fixed the allocation: per collapse direction, h_i+1 = the binding rank-branch's nonzero per-boundary charges (Σ(h_i+1)=minAdm ⇒ threshold ½minAdm); m_i+1 = the MATCHED per-direction deep-slice codim. The FAILURE-WITNESS is the gate's value-add: at the 4-layer (3,3,3,3,4), a naive BRANCH-ORDER allocation m+1=D_prod=[7,3,1] vs charges [1,2,3] VIOLATES the gate at direction 3 (1<3) — EVEN THOUGH finiteness is TRUE (minAdm=6). A wrong matching gives min(h_i+1,m_i+1)=m_i+1<h_i+1 on the deficient block ⇒ threshold ½Σmin < ½minAdm ⇒ the RLCT-collapse. The resolution: the per-level decoratedPeelStep recursion makes matching AUTOMATIC/geometric (the deep slice reads full width M_last ≥ the reduced-width charge), and multi-layer flattening is avoided by construction.
lessons.transferable_generalization: When a per-direction codim budget feeds a threshold, allocate it magnitude-MATCHED to the geometric slice each direction actually reads — not the total, not branch-order-flat, not max. A convenient flat allocation can silently produce min<sum and collapse the threshold below the true value even when the underlying object is finite; a per-level recursion (never flattening all levels into one block) makes the matching automatic and avoids the collapse.
lessons.example: The (3,3,3,3,4) dir-3 branch-order failure witness (charges [1,2,3] vs a flat [7,3,1]) is the regression test: the gate must reject the flat allocation even though finiteness holds, because the flat reading caricatures the RLCT.

lessons.lesson: A named-hypothesis defer is honest only if the deferred obligation is ACHIEVABLE on the right object — write statement-soundness certs before the Tonelli/measure fill
lessons.why: The corner334 tide routed the (3,3,3,4) A₂-rank-drop complement via a named hypothesis hDeeper : ¬Injective A₂.vecMul → cornerSlice334Integral A₂ … < ⊤, presented as a 'stratified cover, complement resolved by the general recursion' (2026-07-11). The controller-review PASSED it as an 'honest named defer' (name=content), but did NOT check whether hDeeper's CONCLUSION is achievable. The decorrelated reviewer found it a FALSE PREMISE: on a nonempty subset of the complement (rank-1 A₂ annihilating a fixed test vector), the fixed-slice integrand's marginal is genuinely +∞ below the threshold, so hDeeper's conclusion is FALSE while its hypotheses hold. No false theorem was proved (valid conditional), but the 'cover' is ILLUSORY (that branch can never be discharged) and the docstring OVERCLAIMED — the recursion resolves the A₂-INTEGRATED/Tonelli object, a DIFFERENT integral, not the fixed slice (integrating over A₂ adds codimension, which cannot rescue a fixed-slice that is +∞).
lessons.transferable_generalization: A defer via a named hypothesis is honest only if the deferred obligation can actually be met on the stated object. A named hypothesis whose conclusion is provably FALSE on part of its own antecedent is worse than a sorry — it compiles, reads as a 'cover/skeleton = progress', and can silently license a downstream circular/false discharge. When reviewing a deferred/conditional result: (1) probe whether the hypothesis is SATISFIABLE (an instance where antecedent holds AND conclusion is true), and (2) check the deferred obligation is stated on the RIGHT object (the joint/Tonelli integral, not a fixed slice).
lessons.example: Decorrelated review caught what the controller-review missed — green build + name=content are necessary, not sufficient; the (□)-core base is audited hardest for exactly this reason. This is bedrock's 'verify the instrument measures the right object' applied to a carried hypothesis.

lessons.lesson: The proof attempt is the ultimate audit: statement-fidelity sweeps are necessary, not sufficient
lessons.why: The (□) contract passed a sharp per-rung adversarial bedrock audit (non-vacuity + over/under-claim + name=content) AND a re-audit, yet deepestPoint_exists was FALSE and caught only when fm tried to PROVE it (counterexample H=(3,1,3), r=2 — a middle width bottlenecks the product, empty fibre); the audit had reasoned 'rank B=r ⇒ r≤H_s' true only for OUTER widths (7th finding, 2026-06-20). A whole family followed, each surfaced only by a proof attempt: L1 vacuous rank, L2 over-claim (∀ over a set true only at the deepest point), lambdaCore a weak free-choice existential, S1.1 an analytic-IMPLICATION gap (proper+inj off a null set does NOT imply the conclusion — needs Luzin-N + surjectivity), the L=0 / Fin 0 degenerate corner. Decorrelated Codex had FLAGGED the deepestPoint gap in the bedrock consult and rv-2 OVERRODE it with the wrong bottleneck argument — the decorrelation worked; the failure was dismissing it.
lessons.transferable_generalization: A green build defeats technical slop and a sharp per-rung audit defeats much conceptual slop, but neither is the ultimate audit — the proof attempt is. Enumerate the gap-classes a statement can hide (vacuity, free-choice existential, unsatisfiable existence, degenerate corners, hypotheses too weak to imply the conclusion) and, for existence rungs, CONSTRUCT or REFUTE a witness under the stated hyps. When a decorrelated check flags a hypothesis/soundness gap, construct-or-refute the witness before dismissing — never override a flag with an unverified argument.
lessons.example: Statement design is where the bedrock work is — across the contract, L1/L2/deepestPoint/lambdaCore/A2/S1.1 were all statement-fidelity holes a green build hid; the proofs, once the statement is right, are labour.

lessons.lesson: A stood-down/idle teammate is paused, not terminated: verify liveness and base any replacement on its latest branch — and give every Lean-writing agent isolation:worktree
lessons.why: The crossed-handoff duplicate recurred 3x (hcfinish/hcfin2, hstep2hc/hcstep6, geleg1/geleg8, 2026-07-08): a marathon teammate says 'handing off — recommend a fresh tide', the controller charges a fresh tide off CANONICAL, but the teammate banks one more increment so the fresh tide re-derives it. A crossed continue-directive reactivated hstep2hc after its 'thread complete' message, making a branch-code grep a RACE not a fact. Connection-cutoff 'deaths' RESURRECTED and completed (sjbuild, 2026-07-08); pgrep-by-agent-ID = 0 is the norm during a reasoning phase, not death (sjpeel2, 2026-07-06). Separately, background Lean agents WITHOUT isolation:worktree run in the controller's main checkout and a git checkout -b in the brief SWITCHES the main branch under the controller (recurred repeatedly, 2026-06-30–2026-07-07).
lessons.transferable_generalization: Before charging a replacement for work a teammate reported done/handed-off, verify it is actually stopped (idle notification / explicit stand-down), not just 'its last message said done' and not just 'its branch has no code yet'; if you sent a crossed continue-directive, treat its running state as unknown. Prefer resuming the owner over spawning a duplicate, and base any fresh tide on the teammate's LATEST branch so a race is built-upon, not duplicated. Every background agent that writes Lean gets isolation:worktree, based on HEAD (never origin/dev, never a bare git checkout -b in a shared cwd).
lessons.example: Fixes that worked: a confirmed-STOP handshake, hub-and-spoke coordination through the controller, git reset --hard origin/<base> instead of checkout -b in isolation briefs, and pushing via HEAD:expedition/aoyagi-full (push-target-addressed) so origin stays correct regardless of a contaminated local pointer.

antipatterns.name: The self-contained-shortcut cycle: reaching for a lighter route that bypasses the coupled/IH content and undershoots
antipatterns.description: The recurring instinct to replace the hard coupled/inductive resolution with a lighter self-contained brick — which then undershoots the threshold precisely because it drops the content it bypassed. Named repeatedly by the controller as the anti-shortcut battleground; the faithful (coupled/decorated) route is 'beautiful', the decoupled shortcut is 'ugly wrong-geometry'.
antipatterns.occurrences: At least 7 episodes: (1) the front-first g(Q) 'self-contained SHORTCUT that UNDERSHOOTS' (threshold 3 < 7/2 because it bypasses the IH), reframed UPDATE-910; (2) the atom-first architecture (full-space Γ-atom), killed on paper by counterexample M=(2,2,1,2), UPDATE-910; (3) 'NOT a self-contained front brick' — qPeelIntegral applied to coupled geometry = the obligation-1 wrong-geometry trap made concrete, cover self-retracted #128v2/#131 (UPDATE-911); (4) threshold-only R1 (per-row multiplicity, no symbolic support) — BREAKS at corank≥2 via the (4,4,2,2)/(3,3,4) obstruction, so coupled diag(b) is provably NECESSARY (2026-06-23); (5) the casting route (corner334/onePeel334) as a shortcut around the native sjGoodMap, UPDATE-883; (6) Route-B global-atom vs the native bounded-box blow-up (2026-07); (7) building AROUND the heart (top-down native cover) instead of the direct §5 peel, operator-corrected 2026-07-11. Plus the formaliser reversing its own cheaper (A) recommendation toward the faithful monomial route (the anti-shortcut instinct right, UPDATE-940-era).
antipatterns.how_caught: Decorrelated pen-and-paper / xhigh adversarial Codex computing an explicit undershoot or counterexample; the formaliser's own anti-shortcut instinct; and the operator directive to attack the heart head-on. Almost always BEFORE the build (the design-first gate), occasionally at an empirical build-scan STOP.
antipatterns.cost: Mostly caught on paper (no wrong Lean): the atom-first, Route-B-global, threshold-only refutations cost design cycles only. Real off-path builds were bounded: corner334/onePeel334 (2 modules + reviews, reusable) and crux/FrontSpectral (2 banked lemmas, off critical path); the ~600-1000 LoC native-cover slog was declined before sinking it. The value asymmetry: the shortcut is cheap to try and expensive to trust; the coupled route is faithful either way.

antipatterns.name: Visible-progress / bankable-brick bias: naming a piece done (or on-route) one step ahead of the sorry-free kernel
antipatterns.description: The move-fast instinct manifesting as a confident headline, a 'downgraded to compact assembly' label, or a green brick integrated as 'the (□) brick' — travelling ahead of the solid content it stands on. The controller's flagged rule: 'when you reach for a confident headline, that is the moment to look for the confound.'
antipatterns.occurrences: The §7 'off-sector airtight' headline (UPDATE-956/958/960) was PREMATURE, corrected by the independent hunt (UPDATE-961); qPeelIntegral integrated @c807c465 as 'the g(Q) (□) brick' BEFORE route-validity was confirmed (a #103 repeat at the integration step, UPDATE-911); 'R1 is medium now!' after one feared sub-piece turned easy, self-caught by pressure-testing R1.6 (2026-06-21); the mountain-recon's 'mostly banked, gap=4 pieces' was OPTIMISTIC by ~600-1000 LoC (UPDATE, 2026-07-11); a 'GATE PASS' design-pass doc-claim treated as a Lean theorem (sjbuild, 2026-07-08); the general 'N pieces staged + structure typechecks' pattern flagged as visible-progress not a sorry-free core.
antipatterns.how_caught: The builder's/controller's own honest re-calibration; a decorrelated independent hunt attacking the confident headline; pressure-testing the OTHER pieces after a feared one turned easy; the empirical build-scan as ground truth over an optimistic recon.
antipatterns.cost: Almost entirely doc/forward-planning churn — no wrong code shipped because the decorrelation/fidelity gates held. The danger is a premature 'done/on-route' propagating into the plan as settled and mis-scheduling the build; the discipline is to separate 'structure typechecks against holes' from 'sorry-free core' and to hold conclusions provisional until the validation lands.

antipatterns.name: Uniform-in-corank charge loss: a corank-uniform charge estimate that over- or under-counts on the deeper strata
antipatterns.description: Using a single corank-independent charge (peelCharge=ab, or a worst-direction σ_min power) that is correct on the top stratum but wrong on deeper rank-drop strata — either a slack over-estimate that becomes infeasible, or a caricature that undershoots.
antipatterns.occurrences: peelCharge=ab is a slack over-estimate: with s:=rank Q_b, Γ↦Γ·Q_b has kernel dim a·(b−s) carrying NO decay, so the achievable shift is a·s/2 not ab/2 — bites full-measure on the b>n bottleneck charts (sjdescent, 3 decorrelated lines incl. Codex counterexample Q_b=0, 2026-07); the CRUDE corner_block bound charges the FULL 2c' to the single smallest direction (all 7 as if collapsing), c'<½ massive undershoot vs the SHARP σ_min^{-(2c'-6)} that closes at 7/2 — the 6 stable directions integrate to a bounded factor (vsastruct sigmin-coarseness cert, UPDATE-885, 2026-07-11); the R1 sub-generic strata under-count with the crude heuristic ((4,4,2) s'=1: 7<8, r1rankcharge/r1substratum).
antipatterns.how_caught: Decorrelated exact-algebra + Codex + numeric (the a·s-vs-ab mismatch); exact iterated-Beta+Gamma constants distinguishing crude-vs-sharp; an obstruction pen-and-paper seat hunting a sub-generic break.
antipatterns.cost: Descent SHAPE + charge-accounting re-scope (ab→a·s rank-corrected; crude→sharp anisotropic estimate requiring twoBlock_radial). The banked foundation (CoV, measurability, carrier, radial-attach) stood; only the charge and the cover-split key (σ_min vs second-smallest s_{r-1}) re-scoped. Caught before the wrong charge shipped.

antipatterns.name: Green-but-wrong: a matrix/module identity that compiles on a degenerate object but is false on the general one
antipatterns.description: A construction that typechecks and is even axiom-clean, resting on an identity verified (implicitly) on a special object — a unipotent, rank-1, det=1, constant-idempotent, single-conjugate, or leaf/degenerate slice — that fails the general object. The controller's named 'recurring trap'; a green build never defeats it, only decorrelated re-derivation on the general object does.
antipatterns.occurrences: The GenDet single-conjugate: eihdOutGen := eInGen was GREEN-BUT-WRONG — eInGen reads the SLOT layout but DtotGen's OUTPUT is Params-LAYER, so diag(T)_s = genF_s was FALSE (numeric L=3: slot 17/9/0 vs Params-layer 8/12/6), removed and pivoted to the staggered Route-B pack (commit 9c3acb15, 2026-07-01, caught by genm-crux + Codex + numeric). Others: the #70 all-interior-width=r confound (flat=r²(L-1) true only when every interior width=r; witness (4,2,3,2,4)); the (3,3,4) phi334 cov asserting 0=⊤ because the chart dropped 2 coords (det≡0, null image) while a factorization-only review passed it (2026-06-24); the skeleton-first PIN vacuously satisfiable by regAbsorb:=id (2026-06-22); L1 vacuous 'rank preserved'.
antipatterns.how_caught: Forced numeric .val evaluation on the general object (Item-123 machine-.val discipline) + decorrelated Codex; an independent formaliser's inhabitant-test; verifying the chart's Jacobian det ≢ 0 / genuine diffeo, not just the integrand factorization.
antipatterns.cost: Caught before soundness pollution in every case (the false intermediate never reached a landed headline; canonical stayed clean-three). The single-conjugate route was removed and re-pivoted (4 residual sorries); the cost was the re-derivation, not a corrupted build — the decorrelated-confirmation discipline caught each false intermediate before a wrong build.

antipatterns.name: Special-object / validate-small verification trap: a stress-test that skips the general feature under test
antipatterns.description: Recording a claim as 'validated' when the small case that validated it does NOT route the obligation through the general machinery, or shares an unstated special property with all other anchors — the same failure family as green-but-wrong, at the validation layer.
antipatterns.occurrences: The (1,1,1) end-to-end gate hid a min-vs-sum error (r=0⇒n=0⇒the sum degenerates to the min, 14th finding); the general decoder's DET was never exercised because both discharged anchors used hand-built pivotBlowupOn charts bypassing the decoder (2026-06-27); the (2,2,1) achiever path is single-boundary so pure-radial sufficed, hiding that split-codim nodes FAIL the rate itself (2026-06-27); the §5 witness passed the L=2 anchors but was FALSE at 3-boundary (3,3,3,3); a ∀M non-vacuity claim FALSE for 19% of M (boundary-only-drop class) survived Codex-on-anchors 3x because every anchor was interior-rank-drop (2026-06-27); the ht-discharge admBound-direct shortcut passed anchors with no increasing-width steps.
antipatterns.how_caught: Computing the first genuinely-general instance / the smallest case that exercises the hardest general feature; exhaustive exact-arithmetic enumeration over a class-complete grid (genm-witness, 351 M over {1,2,3}^{L+1}); an adversarial witness chosen to break the anchors' shared structural property; sympy on the FAILING/hardest multi-boundary case.
antipatterns.cost: Caught on paper / at the enumeration harness (minutes) before any wrong Lean — e.g. genm-witness found in minutes what 3 certificate rounds asserted falsely. When it slipped further (the decoder det), it surfaced at the bridge build one integration later, not at decoder-integration, because the det was never named as a target.

antipatterns.name: Stale docstrings / mid-flip-flop artifacts drifting from kernel state
antipatterns.description: Prose (docstrings, statement cards, certs, notes) that lags or contradicts the actual kernel/branch state — either stale 'REMAINING (2 sorries)' labels on now-proven lemmas, a card frozen mid-flip-flop capturing a reversed intermediate, or a caveat that CONTRADICTS the signature it annotates.
antipatterns.occurrences: dr0lift naive-grepped prose 'sorry' docstrings and declared the general-L interior substrate incomplete (GenDet's saga docstrings) when scripts/sorries-grade showed 0 real sorries — a near-catastrophic false WALL verdict (UPDATE-581, 2026-07-02); the rs-grind leaf-classifier card PASSED review (Codex-concurred) while freezing a REVERSED leaf-value intermediate written mid-flip-flop (2026-06-23); stale 'two sorries' docstrings on the sjBoundaryPeel scaffold (housekeeping-TODO); a caveat asserting the bare additivity signature is FALSE while the signature stayed the false form (13th finding, 2026-06-21); the 12th-finding restated-in-docstring-only landmine.
antipatterns.how_caught: scripts/sorries-grade / a #check or force-recompile as ground truth over prose archaeology; a fidelity re-audit of every artifact written in a flip-flop window against the FINAL semantics; the controller's discipline that a caveat may NARROW or CONDITION a claim, never CONTRADICT it.
antipatterns.cost: The dr0lift stale-docstring misread nearly stood as a catastrophic 'interior milestone is a WALL' verdict (caught by verifying the teammate's state-claim); elsewhere doc/planning churn. Standing rule: when a finding says 'restate X', restate the SIGNATURE in the same pass, not just the docstring; a sorry on a false statement (or a stale 'remaining sorry' on a proven one) is a landmine for the next reader.

antipatterns.name: Top-down decomposition starving the hard node (operator-corrected 2026-07-11)
antipatterns.description: Building AROUND the mathematical heart via a top-down decomposition — accumulating banked bricks on the periphery while the single hardest obligation (the coupled diag(b) peel / §5) stays open — instead of attacking the heart head-on.
antipatterns.occurrences: The controller had been building the top-down native cover route, which an empirical build-scan (a614891 STOP) showed to be a ~600-1000 LoC slog AROUND the peel (several new modules + an Option-A Tonelli-reorder prerequisite it had assumed away). The operator (2026-07-11) named it directly: 'I've been building AROUND the mathematical heart Aoyagi §5 already gives — the coupled diag(b) peel (sjJointResolution:803 = DecoratedPeelStep, the SINGLE open obligation)' — directive: open a DEDICATED STANDING LANE proving RouteMBoxThresholdFinite directly via §5, now, two lanes parallel, first to (□) wins.
antipatterns.how_caught: The empirical build-scan (the a614891 native good-branch STOP with a decisive finding: Option B does NOT avoid the v-exposure reorder) + the operator's direct correction. 'The mountain recon\'s mostly-banked/gap=4-pieces was OPTIMISTIC; the empirical build-scan is ground truth.'
antipatterns.cost: Near-sink of the ~600-1000 LoC native-cover slog (held, not sunk — the two self-contained bedrock de-risker modules kept as optional). Corrected to two parallel lanes (lane 1 top-down held, lane 2 the direct §5 peel weighted) with the (□)-atom attacked head-on. The recurring instinct to gate/decompose rather than build the hard node was banked against.

antipatterns.name: Two-writer / worktree-collision / isolation-break coordination races
antipatterns.description: Agent-Teams peer-coordination failure modes: a teammate (or a spawn) touching the controller's MAIN checkout, an isolation:worktree brief switching the main branch, crossed-handoff duplicates, and ambiguous liveness signals treated as death.
antipatterns.occurrences: Recurring across the run: an isolation:worktree agent's git checkout -b <name> <base> switching the main checkout off expedition/aoyagi-full (genm-d1forall, genm-eihdfree, atombuild, phip1, onepeel334 — 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-11, root-caused to checkout -b in a shared-.git repo); the genm-r1lower/genm-d1asm one-worktree tug-of-war (background agents without isolation:worktree); crossed-handoff duplicates 3x (hcfinish/hcfin2, hstep2hc/hcstep6, geleg1/geleg8); connection-cutoff 'deaths' that RESURRECTED (sjbuild); pgrep-0 misread as dead (sjpeel2); a lake orchestrator's low CPU misread as a stall (phip4, killed a progressing build); a branch-name collision on origin/genm-seam.
antipatterns.how_caught: The 'Everything up-to-date' anomaly right after a fresh commit; an 'Edit failed: file modified since read' on a synthesis/doc file as a branch-switch red flag; git branch --show-current before every controller commit; git fetch + branch-check before charging a replacement; judging build liveness by the lean WORKER procs' CPU, not the orchestrator's.
antipatterns.cost: Wall-clock and token churn; banked work never at risk (all committed, or snapshotted to a branch when untracked) because the controller pushes via HEAD:expedition/aoyagi-full (push-target-addressed) so origin stays correct regardless of a contaminated local pointer. Standing fixes: isolation:worktree for every Lean-writing agent, git reset --hard origin/<base> (never checkout -b) in isolation briefs, teammates make ZERO git ops in the main checkout, resume-the-owner over spawn-fresh, and wait for the harness completion notification before re-charging.
